newsitem.title: AUSTRALIA: RTRS-S.Australia's SAAMC reports A$72.1 mln profit.
newsitem.headline: RTRS-S.Australia's SAAMC reports A$72.1 mln profit.

text.p: The South Australian Assets Management Corporation (SAAMC) has achieved an unaudited after-tax profit of A$72.1 million for 1995/96, up from A$66.8 million in 1994/95, Treasurer Stephen Baker said on Monday.

SAAMC is responsible for the disposal of the non-performing assets of the former State Bank of South Australia, which collapsed in 1991 with more than A$3 billion in accumulated losses, and other assets not transferred to the new BankSA.
BankSA is now fully owned by Advance Bank Australia Ltd.
Baker said in a statement that SAAMC's surpluses were the result of better than expected recovery values achieved from the winding up of the SAAMC portfolio.

SAAMC's total assets, totalling A$8.4 billion in July 1994, had been reduced to A$2.9 billion, comprising property and corporate loans in Australia totalling less than A$500 million, Treasury assets of A$2.4 billion, and offshore assets totalling less than A$30 million, he said.
The reduction included sales of major properties and settlement of corporate accounts totallying A$3.5 billion, he said.
Baker said major assets still held by SAAMC included the 333 Collins Street property in Melbourne and the former State Bank building in Adelaide.
Statutory and legal requirements would not allow a complete wind-down of SAAMC for a number of years, he said.

"However SAAMC's presence will be very low key, with the main tasks now being to finalise payments to creditors as they fall due, manage the wind-down of the remaining subsidiaries, provide information for the ongoing litigation currently in existence, and complete required statutory obligations," he said. -- Sydney Newsroom 61-2 373-1800
